concepts.name: National River Linking Project (NRLP): Origin and Institutional Framework
key_dimensions: Historical genesis: K.L. Rao's Ganga-Cauvery link (1972) vs. Captain Dastur's Garland Canal proposal vs. NWDA's current framework
Role of National Water Development Agency (NWDA) — its mandate, year of establishment (1982), and nodal ministry
Supreme Court's 2012 directive mandating time-bound implementation and formation of a Special Committee
Distinction between NRLP as a concept vs. individual link projects under it — UPSC trap on treating them as synonymous

concepts.name: Peninsular Rivers Development Component: Structure and Key Links
key_dimensions: 16 link proposals under Peninsular component — Mahanadi-Godavari-Krishna-Cauvery cascade linkage as the backbone
Four sub-components: Mahanadi-Godavari links, Krishna-Godavari links, Ken-Betwa (the only link under implementation), and west-flowing rivers of Kerala/Karnataka
Surplus vs. deficit basin identification methodology — UPSC trap: not all southern rivers are deficit basins
Contrast with Himalayan component on feasibility, cost, and ecological sensitivity

concepts.name: Himalayan Rivers Development Component: Structure and Strategic Dimensions
key_dimensions: 14 link proposals including Kosi-Mechi, Kosi-Ghaghra, Gandak-Ganga, Ghaghara-Yamuna links
Dependency on storage reservoirs on Ganga and Brahmaputra tributaries — geopolitical sensitivity with Nepal and Bhutan
Interlinking with flood control objective in Bihar and eastern India — dual purpose (irrigation + flood moderation)
Why Himalayan component is considered more complex than Peninsular: perennial flow, transboundary rivers, seismic zone concerns

concepts.name: Ken-Betwa Link Project: India's First Operational Interlinking Project
key_dimensions: Ken (surplus) → Betwa (deficit): both tributaries of Yamuna — geographic and hydrological rationale
Daudhan Dam as the key storage structure; submergence of Panna Tiger Reserve — biodiversity vs. development tension
MoU signed between MP and UP in 2005; National Perspective Plan inclusion; Cabinet approval in 2021
UPSC trap: Ken-Betwa is under the Peninsular component despite being in central India (Vindhyan region, not peninsular plateau)

concepts.name: Damanganga-Pinjal and Par-Tapi-Narmada Links: Western India Interlinking
key_dimensions: Designed to meet water needs of Mumbai Metropolitan Region (Damanganga-Pinjal) and North Gujarat/Saurashtra (Par-Tapi-Narmada)
West-flowing rivers of Western Ghats identified as surplus — rationale for eastward diversion
Maharashtra-Gujarat interstate dimensions and agreement challenges
Environmental concerns: diverting west-flowing rivers affects estuarine ecosystems and Western Ghats biodiversity hotspot

concepts.name: Concept of Surplus and Deficit Basins: Hydrological Methodology
key_dimensions: NWDA methodology for computing 'utilisable water resources' vs. 'water availability' — UPSC trap on conflating the two
75% dependability criterion used for surplus assessment — what it means and its limitations
Critique: surplus/deficit designation is season-specific and year-specific, not absolute — monsoon vs. lean season variation
Brahmaputra basin identified as having the largest surplus — why it remains largely unharnessed (geopolitics, terrain, ecology)

concepts.name: Interlinking Projects and Interstate Water Disputes: Legal-Political Interface
key_dimensions: Article 262 and Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 as the legal backdrop for disputes that interlinking may trigger
Cauvery dispute dimension: Tamil Nadu's opposition to any diversion from Krishna/Godavari before Cauvery needs are met
Odisha and Andhra Pradesh objections to Mahanadi-Godavari diversion — upstream vs. downstream state conflict
UPSC trap: interlinking does NOT bypass existing tribunal awards — it requires fresh agreements among basin states

concepts.name: Transboundary and Geopolitical Dimensions of River Interlinking
key_dimensions: Nepal's stakes in Himalayan component: Kosi, Gandak, Ghaghra reservoirs require Nepali territory — treaty implications
Bangladesh's concerns: Brahmaputra and Ganga diversion could reduce dry-season flows — 1996 Ganga Water Treaty context
Bhutan's role in storage reservoir construction on Himalayan tributaries
China's upstream projects on Brahmaputra (Zangmu, Motuo) as a complicating factor for India's surplus calculations

concepts.name: Ecological and Environmental Impacts of River Interlinking
key_dimensions: Disruption of longitudinal river connectivity — impact on migratory fish species (Hilsa, Mahseer) and river dolphins
Waterlogging and salinization risks in command areas of interlinked systems — lessons from Indira Gandhi Canal
Wetland submergence: Panna Tiger Reserve (Ken-Betwa), potential impact on Chilika Lake ecology (Mahanadi diversion)
UPSC angle: EIA requirement — Supreme Court's 2012 order mandated environmental clearance for each link separately

concepts.name: Economic Feasibility and Cost-Benefit Analysis of NRLP
key_dimensions: Estimated cost: originally ~₹5.6 lakh crore (2002 prices) — current estimates exceed ₹10 lakh crore with inflation
Projected benefits: 35 million hectares additional irrigation, 34,000 MW hydropower, navigation improvement
Critique by economists: cost-benefit ratio disputed; groundwater alternatives may be cheaper for water-deficit regions
UPSC trap: hydropower generation is a co-benefit, NOT the primary objective of NRLP — irrigation and flood control are primary

concepts.name: Interlinking and Climate Change: Altered Hydrological Assumptions
key_dimensions: NRLP based on historical flow data — climate change altering monsoon patterns making surplus/deficit projections unreliable
Glacial retreat affecting perennial flow of Himalayan rivers — implications for Himalayan component viability
Increased flood frequency vs. extended droughts — interlinking's limited ability to address flash flood scenarios
Need for dynamic water accounting frameworks vs. static surplus-deficit models used in NRLP design

concepts.name: National Water Policy (2012) and its Stance on River Interlinking
key_dimensions: NWP 2012 supports interlinking but emphasizes 'integrated water resources management' as the overarching principle
Policy hierarchy: drinking water > irrigation > hydropower > navigation — how interlinking aligns or conflicts
NWP 2012 vs. Draft NWP 2020: shift toward demand-side management and groundwater recharge over large infrastructure
UPSC trap: NWP is a policy document, NOT a law — it has no statutory force; compare with River Boards Act, 1956

concepts.name: Interlinking and Groundwater Recharge: Indirect Hydrological Benefits
key_dimensions: Canal seepage from interlinked systems contributing to groundwater recharge in arid regions (Rajasthan, Gujarat)
Risk of waterlogging in high water table areas — Punjab-Haryana experience as a cautionary example
Debate: direct groundwater augmentation schemes vs. surface water interlinking for addressing water scarcity
Jal Shakti Abhiyan and Atal Bhujal Yojana as complementary/alternative approaches — UPSC may compare these

concepts.name: Displacement and Social Impacts of Interlinking Projects
key_dimensions: Ken-Betwa project: estimated displacement of ~10,000 families from Bundelkhand — tribal and agrarian communities
Land acquisition under Right to Fair Compensation Act, 2013 — application to interlinking projects
Historical precedent: Sardar Sarovar displacement as a reference point for interlinking project social assessments
UPSC angle: Scheduled Tribes and Forest Rights Act, 2006 applicability to forest land submergence under Daudhan Dam

concepts.name: Role of NWDA: Functions, Mandate and Limitations
key_dimensions: Established 1982 under Ministry of Jal Shakti (earlier Ministry of Water Resources) — a registered society, NOT a statutory body
Core functions: surveys, investigation, preparation of feasibility reports for interlinking links
UPSC trap: NWDA does NOT implement projects — it only prepares DPRs; implementation is by state governments/other agencies
Limitation: NWDA has no power to resolve interstate disputes or enforce agreements — purely a technical body

concepts.name: Interlinking vs. Watershed Management: Competing Paradigms for Water Security
key_dimensions: Watershed management: decentralized, in-situ water conservation vs. interlinking's large-scale inter-basin transfer
Success stories of watershed development: Ralegan Siddhi, Hiware Bazar — contrast with large dam outcomes
Planning Commission (erstwhile) and NITI Aayog positions: endorsement of both approaches but differing emphasis
UPSC angle: watershed management falls under MGNREGS (natural resource management component) — institutional overlap

concepts.name: Mahanadi-Godavari-Krishna-Cauvery Link: The Peninsular Backbone
key_dimensions: Cascading transfer concept: flood surplus of Mahanadi → Godavari → Krishna → Cauvery through a chain of reservoirs and canals
Polavaram Project on Godavari as a critical node — its status as a National Project and current implementation status
Andhra Pradesh bifurcation (2014) complicating water-sharing arrangements for this cascade — new interstate dynamics
UPSC trap: Polavaram is NOT an interlinking project per se — it is a multipurpose project that provides a NODE for future interlinking

concepts.name: Interlinking of Rivers and Navigation: National Waterways Interface
key_dimensions: National Waterways Act, 2016 declared 111 waterways — several overlap with proposed interlinked river corridors
Interlinking canals as potential inland waterways: Ganga-Cauvery axis concept and its navigation potential
Jal Marg Vikas Project (NW-1: Ganga) and its relationship with interlinking infrastructure
UPSC trap: navigation is a tertiary benefit of interlinking, but National Waterways development is governed separately by IWAI under a different ministry

concepts.name: Flood Control Dimension of River Interlinking: North Bihar and Brahmaputra Valley
key_dimensions: Kosi, Gandak, Ghaghra — chronic flood rivers of Bihar; interlinking proposed to divert flood surplus westward
Farakka Barrage experience as a precedent: unintended consequences of river flow modification
Brahmaputra's flood surplus: largest in India — why diversion is geopolitically and technically most challenging
UPSC angle: interlinking for flood control vs. embankments vs. floodplain zoning — different schools of thought in flood management policy

concepts.name: Legal and Constitutional Framework Governing River Interlinking
key_dimensions: Entry 17, State List: water (storage, irrigation) is a state subject — Union's limited direct authority over interlinking
Entry 56, Union List: regulation and development of inter-state rivers 'in public interest' — Parliament can legislate
Supreme Court's 2012 judgment in Networking of Rivers case: directed formation of high-powered committee; PIL filed by Suresh Prabhakar Prabhu
UPSC trap: unlike interstate river water disputes (Article 262), interlinking does not have a dedicated constitutional provision — it relies on legislative competence under Entry 56
